issues.legal_issue: A prior inquiry report that does not adequately resolve responsibility or quantify losses from alleged misconduct by public-sector bank officials does not foreclose an independent further investigation.
material_facts: A judicial commission found serious irregularities in the banks’ grant of a guarantee and criticized the conduct of officials, but did not quantify the losses or the extent of their misfeasance and malfeasance.

A separate report assigned primary responsibility to one official while absolving other officials, although the guarantee had been approved by a board and involved officials at multiple levels; the Court found that report vague and its allocation of responsibility unjustified.
The administrative authority had not taken further action, and the Court had not received a detailed report on the earlier vigilance inquiry because of a technicality.

The Court directed an independent investigation into the losses suffered by the banks, without being inhibited by earlier reports or by the death or retirement of officials, and directed that the existing police report also be considered.
The Court required a status report on the earlier vigilance report and directed completion of the inquiry and filing of a report before the Court.
issues.conclusion: The Central Vigilance Commission was directed to investigate independently the matter, assess the losses attributable to the alleged misconduct, consider the police report, and report to the Court; the inquiry was not to be inhibited by prior reports or by officials’ death or retirement.
issues.legal_principle: Where existing reports do not adequately establish responsibility or quantify loss from alleged misconduct involving public-sector banks, those reports do not prevent the Court from directing a further independent inquiry. The Court relied on no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this direction; it considered the commission’s findings, the limitations and inconsistency of the other report, and the absence of a detailed account of the earlier vigilance inquiry.

predicates.court_proceeding_over_objection_to_an_in: The matter before the Court involved an objection concerning a report about alleged official misconduct.
predicates.alleged_misconduct_by_public_bank_offici: Officials of public-sector banks were alleged to have acted improperly in granting and administering a banking facility.
predicates.existing_reports_leave_loss_unassessed: Existing inquiry reports did not adequately determine or quantify the losses attributable to the alleged misconduct.
predicates.existing_reports_assign_responsibility_i: Existing reports assigned responsibility in a way the Court found inconsistent with the collective and multi-level decision-making involved.

issues.definition: When a court proceeding concerns an inquiry report about alleged public-bank-official misconduct and existing reports leave losses unassessed or assign responsibility inconsistently, the rule calls for an independent inquiry.
